behavior.controller: Owns cached raw/presented input, request/draft identity, request kind and line-prompt presentation. Fresh question guidance returns in curses; discard acknowledgement is neutral and exposes the current request/message prompt. Output invalidates line prompts, which return once after a batch without a trailing newline or insertion during echo.
behavior.drafts: Explicit deletion of a non-stale draft to empty releases live intent. Presentation clears do not release it; stale ownership and original identity last through Enter. Quit/exit, EOF and cancellation remain available. Rejected answers never become messages.
behavior.history: One shared row-byte accounting and omission rule. Complete fitting messages survive; overflow trims complete tokens and reuses existing LF. A truncation whose complete marker cannot fit retains no excerpt. Preparation stops at the retained budget plus fixed lookahead.
behavior.deletion: At most four raw bytes determine a valid scalar or valid trailing prefix. Invalid bytes are individually editable and do not consume preceding ASCII. Rendered escape spelling is not a raw-input deletion unit. Cache tail updates once.
behavior.drawing: Successful native draw statuses are asserted. Connected row/refresh failures grant no review credit. Ordinary errors still retry at the next natural event; scratch-pad acquisition failure still selects ASCII fallback.

negative_controls.drawing_method: Identical tests with temporary header overrides: row-status forces row failure; refresh-credit bypasses require_finish checking. Unmodified control passes, both mutants fail.
negative_controls.boundary_method: Identical ASCII budget and malformed-input probe built against fetched-main and changed inline helpers; baseline fails and changed passes.
negative_controls.prompts: Gated CLI/PTY tests cover approval and question arrival while typing, no answer before acknowledgement, restored current guidance, explicit editing to empty, expiry and later-turn usability.

full_suites.revision_note: Final full suites/static analysis and unit/fault repetitions use 419fb8d production source. Final 3ef24f3 changes only marker-test readiness; all 17 PTY methods are repeated twenty times afterward, and Release measurements use that final ref. Production source equality is asserted.

repetitions.earlier_pty_failure: One prior batch (17) failed after marker creation but before printf content readiness. Failure evidence retained; final marker assertion waits for actual turn completion. No production process/tool code changed.

static_analysis.baseline_equivalence: Fetched main has identical src/include/CMake production files to the prior recorded 2853096 baseline; verified with git diff.
static_analysis.interpretation: Cppcheck passes. Local Clang-Tidy retains five source warnings and one SDK13-incomplete platform translation unit. Clang Analyzer retains the existing context.cpp division warning. Their nonzero status is recorded; no checks or suppressions were weakened. Selftest/canaries pass.

failure_evidence.observation: A final repetition observed an empty approval marker immediately after file creation. The unchanged prior test treated existence as write completion. The final test waits for the completed turn before asserting the exact content; the original assertion remains.
Development PTY test exposed a prompt inserted during keyboard echo. Prompt invalidation is now explicit; idle polling and echo do not schedule fresh prompts.
Initial Linux lint rejected unbound loop callbacks in the new PTY helper. Explicitly bound each callback; final pinned lint passes.

performance.method: Identical Release harnesses and settings: one warm-up and five alternating measured runs, repeated twice, after all local tests/analyzers. No timing thresholds or general speedup claim.
performance.first_comparison: The initial correct accounting used a second prefix scan to back up one complete token. Both first measurement sets show the extra work. The final shared scan returns the previous boundary without re-scanning; all samples are retained.

verification.valid_emoji_deletion: 4096 cache mutations and zero retained-tail preparation on both variants.

performance.counter_limits: C++ operator new and directly interposed calls; not all libc/libedit allocation, hidden writes or peak RSS. prepared_input_bytes counts consumed source for presentation and rebuilt tail bytes for cached input; these are boundary measurements rather than end-to-end keystroke latency.
performance.timing_interpretation: Returning the previous boundary removes the repeat traversal: final large-history medians are 0.436/0.446 and 0.414/0.429 ms baseline/changed, versus first changed medians 0.796/0.782 ms. Exact trimming still adds bounded work: large ASCII/control presentation samples are approximately 7–15% slower than baseline. Validating 4096 emoji deletions takes approximately 0.063 vs 0.042 ms. No blanket latency improvement or timing-based CI threshold is claimed.
